title: Knowledge check: History and Evolution of Vue.js

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “History and Evolution of Vue.js”?
options: Vue requires manual DOM mutation for every state change.
Vue is a database engine for storing server records.
Vue replaces HTML and CSS with a single language.
Vue uses declarative templates and reactive state to keep an interface in sync with application data.
questions.answer_key: Vue uses declarative templates and reactive state to keep an interface in sync with application data.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses History and Evolution of Vue.js directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Origins and design goals”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Vue is a database engine for storing server records.
Vue replaces HTML and CSS with a single language.
Vue uses declarative templates and reactive state to keep an interface in sync with application data.
Vue requires manual DOM mutation for every state change.
questions.answer_key: Vue uses declarative templates and reactive state to keep an interface in sync with application data.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Origins and design goals”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “History and Evolution of Vue.js” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
